This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 17.03.2014 passed in MVC.No.200/2011 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Humnabad (for short 'the Tribunal').
This appeal is founded on the premise of judgment being erroneous and illegal and seeking to set-aside the same.
2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 05.12.2010 deceased Chandrakanth was cleaner of the lorry bearing reg.No.KA.38/5510 which was drive by its driver and both proceeded towards Basavakalyan from Humnabad side and at about 10:30 A.M., when lorry reached in front of Tado Bus stand on NH 9 road, at that time the driver of the lorry drove his vehicle in a high speed and rash and negligent manner to endanger to human life while suddenly over taking to the another vehicle bearing No.MH.43/U7515 has lost control over the said vehicle and dashed to the hind i.e., back side of the said vehicle and thereby caused the accident for which deceased Chandrakanth has sustained grievous injuries and in result died on the spot.
The said Chandrakanth before the accident was hale and healthy and his age was 34 years and by doing the cleaner and agriculture he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Because of the sudden death of Chandrakanth the petitioners are suffering very hardship since they depends upon the income of the deceased.

In view of the sudden and untimely death of deceased,
the petitioners have lost their beloved family member and his earnings.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P8.

On the other hand, respondent did not adduce any evidence and got marked document as Ex.R1.
8.

On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties, Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.8,84,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioner.
The Insurance Company has preferred the appeal to set aside the impugned judgment and award.

9. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellant/Insurance Company that the owner of the lorry bearing No.MH-43/U-7515 in his written statement was not admitted regarding the relationship of employee and employer between the respondent No.1 and deceased.

He further submits that the claimant who has been examined as PW.1 has clearly admitted in the cross-examination that the deceased Chandrakanth was traveling in the said lorry by paying Rs.20/-
to the lorry driver.
Hence, the deceased was unauthorized passenger in the said lorry.
He further submits that the tribunal has tribunal has committed an illegality and perversity the same requires to be set-aside.
Hence, on all these grounds sought for allowing of the appeal.

To substantiate his argument, he relied on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
Vs. Asha Rani and Others, reported in (2003) 2 SCC 223.
10.

Vs. Asha Rani and Others, reported in (2003) 2 SCC 223

sentences.text: Per Contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1-petitioner vehemently contends that the petitioner have filed the petition in the year 2011, till this day, they have not received any compensation amount awarded by the tribunal.
Further he submits that in the FIR it is stated the deceased was working as cleaner of the offending vehicle.

The appellant has not adduced any evidence before the tribunal to discard the evidence of PW.1 and contents of Exs.P1 to P7 and absolutely there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal and there is no scope of interference in the present matter.
Hence seeks to dismiss the appeal preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company.

11. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company and learned counsel for respondent- petitioner.
12.
It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 05.12.2010 and also death of Chandrakanth in the road traffic accident.

In order to prove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioners have produced copy of FIR, marked at Ex.P1. Ex.P1, discloses that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the driver of the offending vehicle.
13. I have perused the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.

sentences.text: In this case the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she reiterated the contents mentioned in the petition.
In support of her contention she has produced 8 documents under Ex.P.1 to P.8.
Ex . P.1 is the C/C of FIR and Ex.P.2 is the C/C of complaint and Ex.P.3 C/C of spot panchanama.
Ex.P.4 is the C/C of inquest panchanama.
Ex.P.5 is the C/C of PM report.
Ex.P.6 is the C/C of IMV report.
After perusal of these documents they clearly disclose that this accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of lorry bearing reg.No.KA.38/5510.
It is relevant to note that, in this case the respondents appeared and they filed their written statement wherein they admitted accident and death of Chandrakanth.
The respondents only denied the age of deceased, income of the deceased.
It is relevant to note that neither respondent nor the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA.38/5510 I have challenged the registration of criminal case before the competent Court of law.
So, the respondents have not at all challenged regarding registration of criminal case against the driver of the lorry.
So, that itself goes to show that, the petitioners have clearly proved that Chandrakanth died in the accident arising out of lorry bearing Reg.No.KA.38/5510 on 05.12.2010 at about 10:30 A.M.,.

The evidence of PW.1 is fully supported by documents, marked as Ex.P.1 to P.6.
Hence, on the basis of evidence of PW.1 which is corroborated by documents.

marked as Ex.P.1 to P.6 and in the absence of any material evidence to disprove Ex.P.1 to P.6,
I hold that, petitioners have proved the Issue No.1 in Affirmative for which I answered the same in Affirmative.

14. Considering the overall facts and documentary evidence placed by the petitioner-respondent No.1, the tribunal has appreciated the evidence on record in a proper and perspective manner and passed the impugned judgment and award.
Hence, there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.

15. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (a) The appeal is dismissed.

(b) The deposited amount, if any, shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal,
along with copy of this order.
